listenings.text: Luiz, it's Megan. The agenda for Thursday has changed. If the flight lands on time, we start at nine. If it does not, we go straight to the credit block at ten fifteen. Two things about the eleven forty block. If Tom asks for a number you do not have, say so and follow up the same day. He has told me that twice. And if lunch runs long, you will lose the site tour, not the credit block. Print nothing.

Luiz, Tom Baker. One request before Thursday. If I ask you something in the meeting and you do not understand the question, stop me. I will say it again in shorter words. That is not a problem. Guessing is. Second, if we run out of time, I will stay for the credit block and drop the targets block. Tell your director that. And if the weather closes the airport, we will do the whole thing on a call, at the same hour.

reading.rtitle: The Question You Did Not Catch
paras: Tom Baker works at headquarters in Chicago. On Thursday he will visit the office in Brazil, and at eleven forty he will meet the credit team for forty minutes. Before the visit, Megan sent the team a short email with three rules.

Rule one: if you do not catch a question, ask Tom to rephrase it. He will not be angry. He has visited twenty offices this year, and he knows his accent is fast. Rule two: if you are not sure, repeat what you understood, so you can clarify it together. For Tom, guessing is the only real problem.

Rule three is about the answer. If Tom asks about the quarterly target, do not say "it is fine". Break the number down: four accounts are late, and all four are distributors. If you do not have a number, say so, and follow up the same day. Most of the revenue arrives after the harvest, so give him a date, not an adjective.
